description: #284 §12.2 — a server-placed function reaches a helper through a FIRST-CLASS REFERENCE (a two-hop alias `const fn0 = sumAmounts; const fn = fn0; return fn(rows)`), not a direct call. loadTotal() runs `SELECT id, amount FROM sales`.all() then sums via the aliased helper. Route inference must ESCALATE sumAmounts server-side (the indirect call is a call edge exactly like a direct one), emit it as an in-process peer, and AWAIT the aliased call. Pre-fix the helper stayed client → the server body referenced an undefined `sumAmounts` → a ReferenceError 500; an unawaited call would ship a Promise. On the real engine @total = SUM(amount) = 35.
rationale: The helper is reached ONLY through a first-class binding (`const fn0 = sumAmounts; const fn = fn0`), so the direct call-graph never sees it. The fix resolves the indirect callee LOCALLY and treats it like a direct call for placement (server escalation), emission (peer callable), and await-lowering (`return await fn(rows)`). The real engine sums the three seed rows (10+20+5) to 35; the stub cannot compute the aggregate, so the value passes ONLY on the real engine and ONLY when the helper actually executes server-side.
